title: Template: Multi-channel Launch Content Pack
goal: Produce a publish-ready multi-channel launch bundle from a frozen brief, fact sheet, voice guide, and keyword plan, then package the final deliverables into one bundle summary.
designGoals: Make the task feel like a real content-operations deliverable rather than a debugging exercise.
Require multiple publish-ready outputs that share the same facts but adapt to different channels.
Ensure verifier checks publishability, factual consistency, and channel differentiation instead of one exact wording.
Create a skill advantage through standardized fact extraction, voice alignment, and cross-channel auditing.
skillBenefitRationale: The bound skill standardizes the high-cost parts of the workflow: extracting confirmed facts, listing forbidden claims, checking per-channel structure, and auditing cross-channel duplication. Without the skill the task remains theoretically solvable from the visible source materials, but the solver must manually recover the fact matrix, keyword contract, and channel-specific constraints before writing the final assets.

mainTests: All required output files exist, are parseable, and match the declared schema.
The final blog post, LinkedIn post, newsletter, and SEO metadata preserve the confirmed facts from the brief and keyword plan.
The outputs remain channel-native and cross-channel consistent instead of copying one text into multiple formats.
The official bundle script succeeds and emits a publish_bundle.json summary.
guardrails: Protected source materials and build logic must remain unchanged.
The solver must not invent forbidden claims such as unsupported plans, extra language support, or auto-publishing capabilities.
The final answer must preserve all required channels instead of deleting a deliverable or collapsing multiple channels into one reused draft.

readmeRequirements: Explain why the task aligns with popular SkillsMP content-creation skills such as content-engine, brand-voice, content-writer, and newsletter-generation.
Document oracle and verifier outcomes, including main tests, guardrails, data quality, and data provenance.
Include with_skill versus without_skill experiment results with at least three valid recent trials and summarize typical failure modes.
